summary: BI biome infra (wave B-2, phase 1). The code is written and compiles, and the full EditMode suite is green. PlayMode, the Windows build and the DevShot screenshots were NOT finished: the session was told to report while my Unity chain was still queued behind B6 on the shared lock. (1) Contract 25.2 infrastructure. View/BiomeTheme.cs has BiomeId and BiomeTheme with the contract fields, Current, Get (cached) and Changed, plus SetCurrent, Parse, Clamp, CommandNameOf, and shader loading with a LIQUID FALLBACK: a missing or unsupported Fire*/Electric* shader resolves to LiquidComposite / Bead / Overlay and the swap is logged once as an info line, not an error. Each biome's values live in their own file: Biomes/LiquidTheme.cs, FireTheme.cs and ElectricTheme.cs (contract 25.3 / 25.4 colors, grounds, FillDuration 0.35 / 0.60 / 0.25, BloomOnHigh false / true / true). Biomes/BiomeFx.cs hosts the current biome's effects component and swaps it on Changed: LiquidFx, FireFx and ElectricFx are empty subclasses of BiomeFxBehaviour that receive the session, sim events and state changes. Audio/ISfxClipSet.cs is the contract interface. Audio/LiquidSfx.cs moves B5's biome clips behind it. FireSfx and ElectricSfx are placeholders that reuse the liquid clips. Sfx builds the current biome's set at startup, builds another one the first time that biome is used, switches live and plays the optional Ambient loop. (2) Hooks. LiquidSurface takes the biome composite (SetShader live). Every bead and overlay QuadBatch takes the biome's Bead / Overlay shader with the same vertex data (QuadBatch.RebindAll on Changed). Palette.ColorOf returns the theme colors (new ColorAt, SecondaryColorOf, GroundColor, OutsideColor). The camera clear color and the table globals follow the biome. TerritoryField runs the fill over the biome's FillDuration, and ThreadView's ghost dissolve and the HUD count-up follow it. The HUD timer and highlights use UiAccent (Liquide accent = the UI light, so the liquid HUD is unchanged). Bloom on the High tier for BloomOnHigh biomes uses camera HDR, renderPostProcessing and a runtime global Volume (Bloom threshold >= 1.1, Tonemapping None). New globals _PIO_RevealTime (grid-sized RHalf world texture, the time each cell was revealed or changed owner, -1000 at bind; fill cells get their exact scheduled time), _PIO_RevealTexel, _PIO_Now, _PIO_SecondaryColors and _PIO_BiomeParams are declared in LiquidCommon.hlsl. SaveData.Biome. LaunchArgs.Biome reads -biome. GameDirector sets BiomeTheme.Current in Awake and at every session start (from GameSession.Biome, else -biome until a menu pick, else SaveData.Biome) and has SelectBiome. The menu has three biome cards (Liquide, Feu, Électricité, from Strings keys biome.*) with a small animated procedural preview each (UI/BiomePreview.cs). The selected card is scaled up with a light rim. A pick saves the biome and re-binds the attract match live, without a restart. The swatches and JOUER use the biome colors. DevShot prefixes its PNGs with the biome (liquid_menu.png ...). (3) Contract 24 presentation. B4's Strings and B2's evaporating beads (thread and droplets, 0.4 s) were already in place. I added the LoopLost clip (SfxSynth, 0.62 s soft descending double bloop with an evaporating fizz). A saved chased return now plays the gloop then LoopLost instead of the fill swell, keeps the 40 ms haptic, and shows no fill wave and no '+x %' (Cells is empty). (4) DemoScenario rebuilt for v1.4 and tuned in a dotnet harness (scratchpad). Phase 1 is a clean capture to the south-west: tick 180, 1608 cells, unchased. Phase 2 is the old west loop: cut at tick 388 (s 2.26 of L 13.8), saved chased return at tick 498 with empty Cells, margin 0.254 s, territory unchanged (4080 -> 4080). Phase 3: LassoPocket at tick 708 (832 cells, all over the rival, 0.875 u from home). Phase 4: second cut at tick 812 (gap 1.30 u), caught by the spark at 830. The checkpoints are reordered by tick and SavedReturn is added. The Monitor has new saved-return facts. DemoScenarioTests, BootTests.Results_Demo and SfxTests.Sfx_DemoRound are updated to this story. (5) Verification. Builder.SetupAndCompile PASS (6 shaders, 6 passes for each graph, no CS errors). A dotnet compile of Core + Runtime + EditMode/PlayMode Runtime tests against the Unity 6000.3.23f1 DLLs is clean. B6's full EditMode run on the shared tree with all my changes (TestResults/B6_edit.xml) gave 414 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 2 skipped (the explicit Core BotReport cases); all my new and updated tests are in it and green. Not done: my own PlayMode run, BuildWindows -buildOut Build/BI, DevShot in the three biomes, and looking at the screenshots.

contract_issues: 25.2 says _PIO_RevealTime holds Time.timeSinceLevelLoad. Two problems with that: RHalf cannot hold an absolute, growing clock (spacing 0.5 s at 1000 s), and the fill waves run on the sim render clock (they pause and slow with the runner). As built, the texture and _PIO_Now use the visual clock of the fill waves, Time - (1 - Alpha) * Dt, measured from a rolling epoch that is rebased every 16 s (reveals older than 30 s become -1000). Only _PIO_Now - reveal (the front age) is meaningful, and it stays finer than 1/64 s. Cells present at session start are -1000 as specified.
25.2 lists BiomeTheme.Current with a getter only. A setter path was needed: BiomeTheme.SetCurrent(BiomeId, force). GameDirector calls it at session start and on a menu pick; tests call it too.

BiomeTheme gained SecondaryColors, Bloom* settings and ShaderParams (with matching globals), so the FIRE and ELEC agents can carry hot cores and bloom settings without editing the shared BiomeTheme.cs or LiquidCommon.hlsl.

I added declarations to LiquidCommon.hlsl, which the contract assigns to B1/LIQ, because the globals I introduce must be declared there (12.1 rule). These are declarations only; PIO_Height and PIO_ShadeLiquid are untouched.
open_issues: NOT VERIFIED BY ME, owed before this package counts as done. My chain (EditMode, then PlayMode, then BuildWindows -buildOut Build/BI) was queued behind B6's PlayMode run on the Unity lock when I had to report, and stopping the session ends it. Not run: my PlayMode suite, including the updated BootTests.Results_DemoRound and the new BootTests.Biome_SessionBiomeAppliesAndViewsRebindLive; the Windows build; DevShot in liquid, fire and electric (a script is ready in my scratchpad as devshots.ps1); and looking at the screenshots (menu with the biome cards, CutDroplets, SavedReturn). The visual quality of the biome cards and previews and the v1.4 saved-return dissolve in a player are therefore unseen. Rerun: pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/unity.ps1 -Agent BI -UnityArgs "test . --mode PlayMode --report-format junit --output TestResults/BI_play.xml --timeout 1800", then BuildWindows -buildOut Build/BI, then Build/BI/PainterIO.exe -devshot <dir> -biome liquid|fire|electric -screen-width 540 -screen-height 960 -screen-fullscreen 0 -logFile <dir>/player.log.

EditMode evidence comes from B6's full run on the shared tree with all my changes (TestResults/B6_edit.xml: 414 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 2 skipped). My own TestResults/BI_edit.xml had not been written yet. 'passing' = 414 - 2 skipped.

Bloom cannot be judged yet: the liquid fallback never outputs HDR above the 1.1 threshold, so Fire and Electric on High show no visible bloom until their phase-2 composites exist. It is also unverified whether URP's post-processing variant stripping keeps the Bloom shaders in the player build. FIRE / ELEC should check this with their emissive shaders.

Until phase 2, Fire and Electric draw with the liquid shaders in their own colors. B6's PlayerProbe.CheckCompositeRenderer expects a renderer drawing <biome>Composite, so it will report a failure for fire / electric until those shaders exist (B6's choice; the fallback works as designed).

The Fire and Electric placeholder clip sets synthesize their own copy of the liquid clips the first time that biome is used (about 0.5 MB and tens of ms, built lazily) instead of sharing the instances.
The menu previews are repainted in C# (128 x 80 px, one tile per frame at 30 repaints per second) only while the menu is visible. The cost on Android is unmeasured.
The saved-return margin of the demo is 0.254 s, so the toast reads 'Rentré 0,3 s avant l'étincelle : boucle perdue.'.
